current_or_implicit_claim: OpenSkill or Bradley–Terry predicts matches better, therefore LOOPR is not very good.
support_status: Not supported; log loss is one construct.
recommended_claim: OpenSkill and Bradley–Terry produce better average probabilities, while LOOPR has a distinct robustness profile for dense-center public ordering.
remaining_limitation: There is no justified scalar weighting these objectives into one winner.

current_or_implicit_claim: LOOPR is the best public ranking.
recommended_claim: LOOPR is a credible ranking-oriented system with unusually graceful degradation in these tests; it does not dominate every baseline or artifact.
remaining_limitation: OpenSkill ordinal has the highest seed-concordance point estimate and Bradley–Terry the best monthly membership retention.

current_or_implicit_claim: LOOPR works equally well across the graph.
recommended_claim: LOOPR is competitive in the dense core and weak at the sparse edge; its intended-use claim must be support-bounded.
remaining_limitation: Core number describes graph support, not every source of uncertainty.

current_or_implicit_claim: LOOPR resists farming and volume inflation.
support_status: Supported for the specified interventions, not universally.
recommended_claim: Repeated weak wins and fivefold evidence duplication moved LOOPR less than the alternatives tested, while strong wins and strong schedules still mattered.
remaining_limitation: Only three weak opponent lineups met the frozen definition; other attacks may exist.

recommended_claim: LOOPR was comparatively volume-resistant under observational and controlled tests; it did not prove exact cancellation.
remaining_limitation: Duplicating evidence can still move rank through global recontextualization.

current_or_implicit_claim: Historical seeds prove LOOPR matches TO judgment best.
recommended_claim: Stored seeds contain meaningful strength information and all four schedule-aware systems agree strongly; the data do not clearly distinguish LOOPR from them on disagreement pairs.
remaining_limitation: Manual/random/copied provenance is absent and automatic seed suggestions are strongly correlated with stored order.

current_or_implicit_claim: The like-for-like incumbent Plus result is cleaner.
recommended_claim: Within-tier/status AUC asks a narrower conditional question; pooled and tier-macro AUC describe the institution that actually operated.
remaining_limitation: Conditioning discards cross-status and cross-tier comparisons rather than purifying them.

current_or_implicit_claim: The pooled Plus AUC is all community skill agreement.
recommended_claim: Pooled AUC is agreement with this vote across all candidates; status and tier explain substantial portions, while LOOPR adds modest out-of-fold information beyond measured institution/activity/support features.
remaining_limitation: Unmeasured reputation and visibility can remain.

recommended_claim: Stability and event-removal robustness are operational requirements for a leaderboard, reported separately from validity evidence.
remaining_limitation: A stable ranking can be stably wrong.

recommended_claim: LOOPR estimates demonstrated ability to convert organized-play opportunities into tournament victories within the observed network.
remaining_limitation: Access, teammate quality, opportunity, and network position may remain in the score.

current_or_implicit_claim: A strong skill-o-meter automatically makes a legitimate public leaderboard.
support_status: Not supported by Part I evidence.
recommended_claim: Part I can establish outcome-derived information and ranking properties; Part II must address named publication, authority, and legitimacy.
remaining_limitation: Exact neighboring ranks and social consequences remain unresolved.
